x: Two who did not win but who fought well were Abigail Gray (one day her front running tactics will pay off in the 1500m) and the stylish young walker Kelly-Anne Parker-Smith.
Two young Belgravians were picked to represent the South of England and both of them, Kelly-Anne Parker-Smith and Nigel Whorlow, walked well to fully justify their selection.

Below: Belgrave's Young Age Groups Walking Team for the Festival of Race Walks in Dublin.
Back row: Lindsay Whorlow, Jonathon Scott, Kelly-Anne Parker-Smith, Susanne Morgan, Jason Stevens, Gary White, Keith McCrudden, Nigel Whorlow, Stephen Whorlow Snr
Front row: Danny Bond, Stephen Whorlow Jnr., Laura Fryer.
Kelly-Anne Parker-Smith took the Under 15 2km road record in Dublin with 11:28 and Lucy Asling the Under 11 1km and 1.2km road and 1000m track records.
Senior, Under 20 and Under 17 Women's 5km 4, K-A.Parker-Smith (2nd U17) 31:37.
Kelly-Anne Parker-Smith was 19th in the Women's 5km (4th U17) and to add to the team's misery of just missing out, Nigel Whorlow also came home 4th in his Under 17 Men's 10km, 15th overall.

Nine year old Lucy Asling again won, helping Belgrave to another clean sweep in the Under 11 age-group, whilst Laura Fryer and Kelly-Anne Parker-Smith both followed up their South of England Championship wins the previous week with further victories.
Under 15 Girls (3,000m.) - Laura Fryer(U13) 10th. Under 17 Ladies (3,000m.) - Kelly-Anne Parker-Smith 4th. Under 15 Boys (3,000m.) - Christopher Stanford 6th.
In the Female 16km event we came eighth, with Laura Fryer (2km), Kelly-Anne Parker-Smith (6km), Victoria Parker-Smith (4km) and Sue Porter (6km) making up the team.
